questions.stem: The INTERGOVERNMENTAL PANEL ON CLIMATE CHANGE (IPCC) was established by:
questions.explanation: IPCC founded in 1988 by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) and the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP). HQ: Geneva. Assesses scientific literature on climate change. Latest Assessment Report: AR6 (2021-2023). Nobel Peace Prize 2007 (shared with Al Gore).

questions.stem: India's commitment under the PARIS AGREEMENT includes achieving NET-ZERO EMISSIONS by the year:
questions.explanation: India announced at COP26 (Glasgow, 2021) — 'Panchamrit' commitments: net-zero by 2070. Also 500 GW non-fossil installed capacity by 2030, 50% renewable electricity by 2030, 1 billion tonne emission reduction by 2030, reduce carbon intensity of economy by 45% below 2005 levels.

questions.stem: The Paris Agreement aims to limit global average temperature rise (compared to pre-industrial levels) to:
questions.explanation: Paris Agreement (COP21, December 2015): cap warming 'well below 2 °C', pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5 °C. IPCC's SR1.5 report (2018) made the case for 1.5 °C. NDCs = Nationally Determined Contributions, submitted every 5 years.

questions.stem: The International Solar Alliance (ISA) was launched by India along with:
questions.explanation: ISA — co-founded by India and France at the COP21 Paris summit (Nov 2015). HQ: Gurugram, India. Aim: promote solar energy, especially in 'Sunshine Countries' between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn. As of 2023, 100+ member countries.

questions.stem: The KYOTO PROTOCOL (1997) introduced the concept of:

options.option_text: Binding emission-reduction targets + carbon trading mechanisms

questions.explanation: Kyoto Protocol — adopted 1997, came into force 2005. First commitment period 2008-2012. Introduced three flexible mechanisms: International Emissions Trading (IET), Clean Development Mechanism (CDM), Joint Implementation (JI). Superseded effectively by Paris Agreement.

questions.stem: Which gas has the HIGHEST global warming potential (GWP) per molecule (over 100 years)?
questions.explanation: GWP (100-yr) approximates: CO₂ = 1, CH₄ ≈ 28-34, N₂O ≈ 273, HFCs 1,000s, SF₆ ≈ 23,500 — one of the highest. Used as electrical-insulator in switchgear. Lifetime in atmosphere ~3,200 years.

questions.stem: 'COP' in 'COP27 at Sharm El-Sheikh' stands for:
questions.explanation: COP = Conference of the Parties — to the UNFCCC (United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, 1992). COP1 Berlin 1995, COP21 Paris 2015, COP26 Glasgow 2021, COP27 Sharm El-Sheikh 2022, COP28 Dubai 2023.
